content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint lacks explicit estimand attributes",
      "quote": "The primary efficacy endpoint for this study is the ORR as determined by central review.",
      "page": 34,
      "section": "4.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint is stated but the estimand is not fully specified: population (Group 1/Group 2), variable (ORR), intercurrent events (e.g., death, progression before response, treatment discontinuation) and summary measure (proportion) are not explicitly defined. This is a key gap for regulatory alignment.",
      "fix": "Add an estimand section specifying population, variable, intercurrent event handling (e.g., treatment policy, composite), and summary measure for the primary endpoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoints lack analysis details",
      "quote": "The secondary endpoints are: Duration of response, PFS, OS, CR rate, Change in scores of patient-reported outcomes in the EORTC QLQ-C30 and the Skindex-16, AEs, Concentrations of cemiplimab in serum (at select sites), Anti-cemiplimab antibodies",
      "page": 34,
      "section": "4.2.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The secondary endpoints are listed but no analysis methods are described for them in the statistical plan section. For example, how DOR, PFS, OS, CR rate, PROs, safety, PK, and immunogenicity will be analyzed is missing.",
      "fix": "Provide analysis methods for each secondary endpoint, including estimands, statistical models, and handling of missing data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of intercurrent events for ORR",
      "quote": "Patients who are deemed not evaluable by RECIST version 1.1 (Group 1; Appendix 1) or by the composite response criteria (Group 2; Appendix 2) will be considered as not reaching PR/CR for ORR.",
      "page": 34,
      "section": "4.2.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The handling of non-evaluable patients is stated, but other intercurrent events such as death before response assessment, treatment discontinuation due to toxicity, or use of subsequent therapy are not addressed. This could bias the ORR estimate.",
      "fix": "Define how all intercurrent events (e.g., death, discontinuation, subsequent therapy) are handled in the estimand for ORR."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing data handling not specified",
      "quote": "The final SAP will be issued before the database is locked.",
      "page": 82,
      "section": "10",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical plan defers details to a future SAP, but the protocol should at least outline the approach for missing data (e.g., for PROs, missing responses, censoring rules for PFS/OS). Currently no missing data handling is described.",
      "fix": "Add a section on missing data handling for all endpoints, including sensitivity analyses."
    },
    {
      "title": "Multiplicity not addressed for multiple endpoints and groups",
      "quote": "For the primary endpoint of ORR, the statistical hypothesis is that cemiplimab-treated patients will have an ORR representing a clinically meaningful treatment, with Group 1 and Group 2 evaluated independently.",
      "page": 82,
      "section": "10.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not discuss control of Type I error across the two primary analyses (Group 1 and Group 2) or across secondary endpoints. This is a common regulatory requirement.",
      "fix": "Specify the multiplicity strategy (e.g., hierarchical testing, alpha allocation) for primary and secondary endpoints."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size inflation inconsistent with stated power",
      "quote": "The sample sizes will be further increased by 5% to account for patients who withdraw prematurely from the study. Hence, the total sample sizes will be 53 patients for Group 1 and 84 patients for Group 2, for a total of 137 patients.",
      "page": 82,
      "section": "10.2",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol states 50 and 80 patients are required for power, then inflates by 5% to 53 and 84. However, the power calculation is based on the original sample sizes, and the inflation may not preserve the stated power if the analysis uses the inflated sample size. Also, the 5% inflation is not justified in terms of power.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether the power calculation accounts for the inflation or if the analysis will use the original sample sizes. Provide justification for the inflation rate."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoints lack analysis methods",
      "quote": "The following exploratory analyses are planned: Associations between tumor non-synonymous mutational burden at baseline and efficacy of cemiplimab",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "4.2.3",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Exploratory endpoints are listed but no statistical methods are described for them, such as correlation tests or regression models.",
      "fix": "Add brief analysis methods for exploratory endpoints, even if descriptive."
    },
    {
      "title": "Interim analysis details incomplete",
      "quote": "An interim analysis of Group 1 patients will be performed at the time of the primary analysis for Group 2.",
      "page": 82,
      "section": "10",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The interim analysis is mentioned but no details are given on the analysis scope, decision rules, or whether alpha will be spent. This could be an amendment risk.",
      "fix": "Specify the interim analysis objectives, endpoints, and any stopping or futility rules."
    }
  ]
}
